Read a performance table from file

Source: R/performance.R
readPerformance.Rd

Reads a performance statistics table previously written by writePerformance(), restores column classes, keying, and column order, and returns the result as a data.table.

readPerformance(file = "model/performance.dat.gz")

Arguments

file

A character string giving the path to the performance table file. Defaults to "model/performance.dat.gz".

Value

A data.table containing performance statistics. The returned table:

  • has columns coerced to the expected classes;

  • is keyed by om, type, run, biol, mp, statistic, and year;

  • has columns ordered as om, type, run, mp, biol, statistic, name, desc, year, iter, data;

  • converts grouping columns such as om, type, run, mp, biol, statistic, and label to factors when present in the file.

Details

This function is the standard reader for performance tables stored on disk, typically in compressed text format such as model/performance.dat.gz.

The function uses data.table::fread() to import the table and explicitly sets classes for commonly used columns in performance output:

  • type, run, mp, and biol are read as character;

  • year and data are read as numeric;

  • iter is read as character.

After reading, a key is assigned with data.table::setkey() to facilitate fast joins and subsetting. The function also standardizes column order so downstream utilities can assume a stable structure.

If a label column is present in the file, it is converted to a factor along with the other categorical columns.

See also

mse::performance() writePerformance(), summaryPerformance(), labelPerformance()

Author

Iago Mosqueira, WMR

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Read the default performance table
dat <- readPerformance()

# Read from a specific file
dat <- readPerformance("results/performance.dat.gz")

# Inspect the structure
str(dat)
key(dat)
} # }
